questions.q: Who does Yahweh tell to pay attention?
questions.a: Yahweh tells the priests, the people of Israel, and the members of the royal court to pay attention because he is going to judge them.

questions.q: What have the revolters done, and what will Yahweh do to them?
questions.a: They have killed many people, and Yahweh will punish all of them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about Ephraim and Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh says he knows that they have been unfaithful to him by worshiping idols and have made themselves unacceptable to him.

questions.q: What will not allow Ephraim to return to their God?
questions.a: The evil things Ephraim has done will not allow them to worship their God any more.

questions.q: What will happen to Israel, Ephraim, and Judah because of their sin?
questions.a: The people of Israel, Ephraim, and Judah will fail because of how much they have sinned.

questions.q: Why will the people not find Yahweh?
questions.a: The people will not find Yahweh because he has removed himself from them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to them when they bring their sacrifices to the festival?
questions.a: Yahweh will kill them, because they have betrayed him and do not belong to him.

questions.q: Where should the trumpet and horn be blown?
questions.a: The horn should be blown in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah, and the alarm sounded at Beth Aven.

questions.q: Who declared that Ephraim will become a desolation?
questions.a: Yahweh declared that Ephraim will become desolate when he punishes them.

questions.q: On whom will Yahweh pour his wrath?
questions.a: Yahweh will punish the leaders of Judah because of his wrath.

questions.q: What will happen to Ephraim when Yahweh judges them?
questions.a: The people of Ephraim will suffer greatly because they were determined to worship worthless idols.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to Ephraim and Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh will destroy the people of Ephraim like a moth destroys wool, and he will destroy the people of Judah like rot destroys wood.

questions.q: When did Ephraim go to Assyria?
questions.a: When Ephraim saw that their nation was weak, then they went to Assyria for help.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to Ephraim and Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh will cause soldiers to kill many of them and carry the others away, and there will be no one to rescue them.

questions.q: For how long will Yahweh leave them to themselves?
questions.a: Yahweh will leave them to themselves until they admit that they have sinned and that they need him to forgive them; until they earnestly ask him to help them.

commentary.text: The Divine judgments against Israel. (Hos. 5:1-7) Approaching desolations threatened. (Hos. 5:8-15)

Hos. 5:1-7 The piercing eye of God saw secret liking and disposition to sin, the love the house of Israel had to their sins, and the dominion their sins had over them. Pride makes men obstinate in other sins. And as Judah was treading in the same steps, they would fall with Israel. By dealing treacherously with the Lord, men only deceive themselves. Those that go to seek the Lord with their flocks and their herds only, and not with their hearts and souls, cannot expect to find him; nor shall any speed who do not seek the Lord while he may be found. See how much it is our concern to seek God early, now, while it is the accepted time, and the day of salvation.

Hos. 5:8-15 The destruction of impenitent sinners is not mere talk, to frighten them, it is a sentence which will not be recalled. And it is a mercy that we have timely warning given us, that we may flee from the wrath to come. Compliance with the commandments of men, who thwart the commandments of God, ripens a people for ruin. The judgments of God are sometimes to a sinful people as a moth, and as rottenness, or as a worm; as these consume the clothes and the wood, so shall the judgments of God consume them. Silently, they shall think themselves safe and thriving, but when they look into their state, shall find themselves wasting and decaying. Slowly, for the Lord gives them space to repent. Many a nation; as well as many a person, dies of a consumption. Gradually, God comes upon sinners with lesser judgments, to prevent greater, if they will be wise, and take warning. When Israel and Judah found themselves in danger, they sought the protection of the Assyrians, but this only helped to make their wound the worse. They would be forced to apply to God. He will bring them home to himself, by afflictions. When men begin to complain more of their sins than of their afflictions, then there begins to be some hope of them; and when under the conviction of sin, and the corrections of the rod, we must seek the knowledge of God. Those who are led by severe trials to seek God earnestly and sincerely, will find him a present help and an effectual refuge; for with him is plenteous redemption for all who call upon him. There is solid peace, and there only, where God is.
